messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Stan Autodiff/Math Library Name
parts:
When we pull the autodiff/math code out into a separate repo we need
to give it a name. I called the second-generation code “Nomad” to play
on the “AD” but we need not be as playful here. Anybody have any
strong opinions? I can offer

SADLib (Stan Automatic Differentiation Library — logo is just the sad emoticon :-( )
StanAD
StanADE (Automatic Differentiation Engine)

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Stan Autodiff/Math Library Name
parts:
As much as I like Aki's suggestion, I like simple, as in:

StanMath

though camel case has perhaps seen better days, so
maybe

The Stan Math Library

In particular, I would rather reinforce than split the
Stan brand. I find the Sacado (autodiff) as part of
Trilinos (larger math lib) thing really confusing.

If Andrew insists on throwing SEO and branding to the
wind, and we have to go with a name, we could use "Mike"
in the spirit of "Stan" --- it was the code name of
the first hydrogen bomb test and also a riff on Michael :-)
Or Edward after Teller if we want to full nuclear, or maybe
Nicholas after Metropolis (though it's the piece w/o
Metropolis!)

Now that Betancourt's in London, maybe he can nip down to
the East End for some help with some Cockney rhyming slang,
which is easiest to explain with an example:

Water Closet -> Waterloo -> loo

From Wikipedia:

One example is replacing the word "stairs" with the rhyming
phrase "apples and pears". Following the pattern of omission,
"and pears" is dropped, thus the spoken phrase "I'm going up the
apples" means "I'm going up the stairs".

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Stan Autodiff/Math Library Name
parts:
Since we're lobbying, I'm not a big fan of forced acronyms,
sampling through adaptive neighborhoods aside, of course.
I love that one.

I'm also not a big fan of "engine" or "toolbox" or "box"
or "works" or anything else industrial age.

By comparison, both Boost and Eigen refer to themselves
as "libraries". First thing on their home pages:

"boost C++ libraries"

"Eigen is a C++ template library..."

I like the quaintness and directness of "library". No idea
why Boost lowercased "boost" on their web header, since it's capitalized
everywhere else in their doc and all-caps on their red download button.

- Bob
